item.title: Re: (Looking for greenlight) The Ever-Hunger
item.content:encoded:
So… what you are suggesting is that the narrative is too wide(?) with a lot of stuff that didn't get dived into, right?.

I think maybe I should cut off some unnecessary stuff eg exploration logs, interview? or maybe I should explain/dive into each aspect of the lores differently (like Infohazard from communication logs?, anti-memetic in incident logs involving other SCPs? etc. An O5 "summary" at the end in the form of message?).
I would love to hear your suggestion on this before I return to my Ipad draft and try to write it out more carefully. (Do I have to post the fixed version in this thread? or do I make a new one?)

Thank you for your critique.

item.title: Re: (Looking for greenlight) The Ever-Hunger
item.content:encoded:
I'm,,,somewhat conflicted on this. The Elevator Pitch introduces a lot of intriguing elements, particularly around it actively consuming information; but my concern is that the actual narrative here feels…like it doesn't really go anywhere interesting.

Really, I'm just kinda looking at the various writing elements you're using (the experiment logs, the mtf explorations, the interviews, the failed neutralisation etc etc) and feeling like there's a lot of stuff going on that doesn't really collapse into feeling like it's telling one coherent story so much as just like, throwing in a lot of elements in an attempt to see what parts stick.

This kinda feels like it touches on a lot of parts of site lore ('Pataphysics via the authors coming in, antimemetics from the behaviour of the scp, pattern screamers via the black voids it leaves behind) without really doing anything new with the elements beyond just kinda mentioning them; and I'm not sure how much of this is an issue per se except in that you don't really do a lot narratively with this.

item.title: (Looking for greenlight) The Ever-Hunger
item.content:encoded:
An anomaly that gradually consumes its designated slot and neighboring SCPs in the database, causing them to "cease to exist".

I moved and trimmed your thread summary, since it was taking up extra space in the main forum screen. Try to keep thread descriptions (the text in the little box under the thread title) and titles short so you don't crowd out other authors in the forum listing. ~Zyn

Seeking Greenlight Yes
Page Type SCP Article
Genre Horror

+ show block
– hide block

Elevator Pitch
This anomaly does not have an appearance but from signs of consuming its designated slot and neighboring slots through usages of biting and tearing texts and images apart.

The document/data concerning this entity must be periodically moved to a different slot when signs of consumption and degradation start to show in the file.

If the entity does not get relocated, then it will start devouring neighboring SCPs documents (causing fading memory, anti-memetic effect) and, "deleting" them from the database" and literally, making them become non-existent along with related sites, staff, and personnel.

This SCP is not a virus in the database as it has the ability to erase things it consumes from existence in the SCP universe. The location where the deleted site/anomalies used to be will be replaced with a black void, signifying a hole in reality itself. Because of the reality bending effects it left, it is designated an infohazard/cognitohazard Keter anomaly. Observing the tear in reality caused the observers to become "aware" of its fictional status, and aware of entities from higher dimensions (the authors) who have the power to influence and shape their universe.

This ever-hunger entity can cause an end-of-reality scenario if left unchecked, so the O5 planned to cause global extinction in case of a breach.

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative (Ignore this one: old edit)
—This will be presented by normal means of containing, describing this as an extradimensional SCP (A normal stuff in SCP) & (constant relocation "procedures" of the anomaly) while hiding its true nature (that it cannot be permanently contained and that it caused things to become non-existent). And fake description/containment procedures to keep people from panicking and becoming aware of their fictional world. This implies that in the future, it may devours its designated slot faster than the foundation could even react. Maybe this SCP has a connection with SCP-055 as its origin point?

Experimental logs involving D-Class getting send into the void, MTF getting erased from the database as they explore the deleted site and list of "known" deleted anomalies that the foundation somehow still have the record.—

+ show block
– hide block

Central Narrative

A message from the overseer saying to all sites of reports of a mass reality shifting, and assuming that somewhere there's a reality bending entity of immense magnitude entering the PRIME/main dimension. They then send an order for every team to investigate where/what happened.

O5-1 then send an email to the O5 linking an "exploration/field log (just the file name, the real one will come later on in the story)" telling his council members to go investigate.

A level 5 encrypted message is then sent (a few days later) through the database though the message is halted/corrupted beyond understanding, the intangible part saying only that they must send every team, every personnel and every anomalies they have as "the database must not be breached".

Then the SCP document is presented with Keter containment class.
The document says that it must be contained at a site constructed at the Overwatch command (AKA the secret place where the O5 meets and stuff?) and its "cell" encrypted with many layers of encryption only the O5 has access. To prevent "breaching" of containment. In case of a containment breach then protocol (Expunged. Later reveals to be global extinction AKA the SCP-5000 story through Pietro Wilson journal at the last part)

The description is locked under level 5 warning saying that the SCP is an infohazard.
The whole document is just normal reality-bending anomaly SCP stuff that doesn't seem to even be an infohazard at all, ending with a discovery log of a team that, as O5-XX said, isnt named anywhere at all in the SCP database (implying that they got wiped from existence)"
The log (as mentioned above) is full of redacted and expunged stuff when its talking about the things the team saw, the things they realized.

Then an attempted level 5 login by an underleveled researcher but he got caught and brought to the O5 council.

In the interview log, he said that he suspected that the document itself isn't an infohazard, but by piecing together the act of "encrypting its cell" with many layers of codes and the vague discovery logs, it is clear that the O5 doesn't want the "entity" to break out, but from outsider to break in. He said that this is unprofessional and different from the motto of the SCP foundation "Secure-Contain-Protect", and that the O5 are trying to use this SCP to their own gain. End of Interview, the researcher fate is left unknown.

Then a message from O5-1 to all O5, with an inspection log of the SCP, written by O5-1, for the first time in a years, followed by an incident report of many SCPs (Numbers like 8XXX, 7XXX etc) starting to gain anti-mematic effects.

Next is a message from the O5 council to the Administrator, saying that someone has been imposing as O5-1, as O5-1 doesn't exist and that "the spot has been empty since forever."

Then the document (updated a few days ago) of literally the same SCP document but with changed item numbers, followed by a document from O5-2 to the O5, jokingly starting with "I blocked that imposter -1 dude, dunno if he's been located yet".

O5-2 stated a list of SCPs-xxxx that has entirely been "neutralized", though the SCPs have gained the property of "space-time" anomalies, changing into a form of void like shaped. The effect of all these anomalies are "cognitohazard/mematic" inducing a form of idea in an individual mind, stating that "they are not real. They wrote us, the authors wrote us into existence".

O5-2 invites all the O5 to check the anomaly contained at Overwatch command, mainly inspected by O5-1 (whom everyone forgotten).

2 documents: the 1st one is the original document from the beginning, all blank.
the 2nd one, the document with the new number, starting to go blank.

3rd document: locked with level 5 clearance//Infohazard/Mematic document saying that this anomaly must periodically be assigned to a new SCP number. The description only said that it is a trans-dimensional entity which consumes its slot before devouring other SCPs in the database, anomalously, making the SCPs ceased to exist.

A note from O5 council, ordering that an amnestic must be given to related staff and personnel if an SCP has gotten wiped from existence to prevent mass confusion and utter chaos.

The anomalies must be prevented from viewing (by covering/build a site over it) and those who have viewed it and gained the mematic effect must be terminated only.

A note from O5-2 to the rest of the council says that he will lead an experiment to end their debate if whether of not this data-consuming SCP and the disappeared SCPs has any correlation.

A live broadcast transcript from O5-2 starting with him observing the current document, and reporting changes in the document as time goes by.

As the document fades to emptiness, he observes the affected SCP.
Then he starts saying things like how it's weird to imagine oneself living in a cartoon world. Everything is all real to the residents until the animator decided to erase drawings and maybe tear the paper in the process, how would the residents of the cartoon world perceive the erasing, seeing black? Seeing "nothing"?

He reports feeling the same thing, before going radio silent for longer than an hour.
He begins laughing frantically, saying that they're lucky "the authors" wrote them to have powers in this universe, not like the D-Class getting their femur broken like toys.
He order to release and broadcast the void/the truth to the global populations.

Then a message from O5-6 to O5 except 1,2 for an emergency meeting of a database breached by the GOC. He emphasize that O5-2 must've relayed the information to the GOC and if the SCP is not relocated, then all the SCP will be wiped out and the damage will be too severe.

Before everything goes out of control, the council decided that the best way to prevent utter removal of the SCP universe is to either "neutralize the SCPs and its creator through memetic agents into their dimension (SCP-5999)" or to wipe out humanity like O5-1 proposal, saying that if this world ends then the other writers would write them up to existence in another canon anyway.

A broadcast by the Foundation (Same picture as SCP-5000) is broadcast worldwide.
A section of Pietro Wilson's story is written at the end, implying that this happens in the same scenario as SCP5000.

+ show block
– hide block

Hook/Attention-Grabber
The document ending will be left vague after all the interviews, logs, failed neutralization attempt and how the GOC tried to use this anomaly without knowing the after-effect. This will left the reader to imagine if they all died (from O5 explosion), wiped out from the conflict between GOC and the foundation, or something else entirely.

Update: with the new core narrative I think the hook would be changed to a story told through imagination by jumping from logs to logs and having the reader imagines what happens (Ex: the fate of the researcher and what happens to O5-1)

Additional Notes
None
